title: Marco Rose appointed Bournemouth head coach: A manager committed to a courageous style of play
content:
Bournemouth have reached an agreement to appoint Marco Rose as their next head coach, with the German to succeed Andoni Iraola when he departs the club at the end of this season.

Following news last week that Iraola would be leaving when his contract expires in June, Rose emerged alongside Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna as a leading contender for the role.

Extensive background work had already been undertaken and that enabled Bournemouth to conclude the process rapidly, ensuring minimal disruption for their remaining Premier League games and efforts to achieve European qualification for the first time in the south coast side’s history.

Despite not having previously worked in England — as was the case with Iraola — Rose’s vast experience of continental competition proved a vital reason why he became the chosen option.

A playing style bearing similarities to that which Bournemouth currently exhibit was another crucial factor, while helping develop the likes of Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Dominik Szoboszlai also carried weight for Rose, 49.

He will take over from Iraola on a three-year contract and once the new coaching staff begins to form it is expected to combine members of his own backroom team with some nurtured internally.

Significant time has been spent planning for this moment, much how Bournemouth have shown themselves capable of losing key players but replaced them well and continued to progress.

That said, they intend to keep all of their star names in the upcoming summer and give Rose the best chance of success. A number have deals that include release clauses but Bournemouth do not anticipate those being activated and their financial position should enable them to avoid unwanted sales.

Rose was a fixture in the German Bundesliga for six years across spells with Borussia Monchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, having previously coached Red Bull Salzburg to successive Austria Bundesliga titles.

Bournemouth are currently eighth in the Premier League but are level on points (48) with sixth-place Chelsea and Brentford, in seventh. Last season, Iraola led Bournemouth to their highest top-flight points total (56) and a joint-high ninth-place finish.

Iraola’s side are next in action when they host Leeds United on Wednesday.

Analysis by football data writer Thom Harris

Marco Rose has been out of a job since he was dismissed by RB Leipzig in March 2025, but was a leading proponent of the high-pressing football at the Red Bull multi-club network, currently overseen by former Liverpool coach Jurgen Klopp.

Gegenpressing is at the heart of the group’s tactical model — looking to win the ball back quickly after losing it, something that clearly appeals to Bournemouth.

At their best, Rose’s Leipzig side were an intimidating force, going 16 unbeaten, winning the German Cup and averaging over 2.0 goals per game throughout his first season in charge. He got the best out of attacking talents Xavi Simons, Benjamin Sesko and Lois Openda; no Bundesliga side took more shots (90) or scored more goals (23) via fast breaks while the Austrian was in charge.

Volatility is inherent in the Red Bull model, built upon a rotating cast of young players with high potential who can take time to settle or suffer from losses of form. Rose struggled to turn the tide when results faltered in winter 2024, finding it hard to impose his all-or-nothing style on a weakened squad lacking in athleticism and confidence in midfield.

That said, Rose’s pedigree has rightly attracted Bournemouth, a manager with 45 games under his belt in the Champions League, a double title-winner in Austria, and with four top-four finishes in the German top-flight to his name across three different clubs.

His commitment to a courageous style of play — vertical, aggressive and fast — clearly gels with a team who have consistently punched above their weight, approaching their football in much the same way.
